topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecturer, sets out the scope of the cancer lecture series, and outlines the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Conceptual foundations and epidemiological evidence of cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the genetic and evolutionary nature of cancer, debating the relative contributions of endogenous cellular errors versus environmental and geographic factors.

topics.label: Infectious agents and oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: They detail how viral, bacterial, and parasitic pathogens drive cancer, highlighted by the case study of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical, dietary, and physical mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: They describe how specific chemical, dietary, and radiation exposures directly damage DNA or require xenobiotic activation to induce mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how non-mutagenic factors like chronic inflammation, chemical promotion, and host developmental stages contribute to carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for determining carcinogenicity and assessing risk
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss the sequencing, epidemiological, and experimental methods used to identify carcinogens, concluding with the practical challenges of evaluating human exposure risks.
